tours.title: Aburi, Ghana Private Zipline and Adventure Experience
tours.description:
This four-hour trip from Accra combines a waterfall, a ropes course and a stop at the Aburi craft market in one morning or afternoon. The setting is the Akuapem hills, where the Asenema waterfall runs down through forest, and the air is noticeably cooler than in the city.

The adventure course is the main event. You are fitted with safety gear and clipped onto interconnected ropes for a route that rewards people who are reasonably fit. This is not a gentle walk: the operator asks that you exercise regularly and sets a minimum age of 16 and a minimum height of 1.5 metres. Anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a supervising adult who takes part in the activity.

After the course, the day slows down at the Aburi craft village, where you can browse carvings, textiles and souvenirs made by local artisans.

Private transport from Accra is included, in an air-conditioned saloon car for one to three people or a van or bus for larger groups, along with fuel, bottled water, the entrance fee and a guide. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes you can move in.

Good to know: about four hours, minimum age 16 and height 1.5m, under-18s need a participating adult, a reasonable fitness level is required, private air-conditioned transport from Accra, entrance fee, bottled water, guide, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra Culture Walk: Fantasy Coffins, Art Gallery & Beaches
tours.description:
Accra's art and its funeral culture are closer than they look, and this three-hour walk covers both in the cooler part of the day. The start is deliberately late: the midday heat has gone by the time you set off, and the route ends at the coast around sunset.

The first stop is the Artists Alliance Gallery, which overlooks the ocean. You spend over an hour across its three floors, looking at paintings, sculpture and Kente cloth. Your guide puts the work in context and gives you room to look rather than rushing the rooms.

A short walk brings you to a fantasy coffin workshop. In Ghana, funerals are celebrations of a life, and coffins are carved to represent what the person loved: a giant trainer, an aeroplane, a fish, a luxury car. You meet the artisans, hear how the tradition began and see why it is known far beyond Ghana. This is the part of the walk most people photograph.

You finish with a drink — a fresh street coconut, chilled sobolo or a beer — at a beachfront club, in time for the golden hour.

The route is on foot, so wear comfortable shoes. Bring a camera and sunscreen.

Good to know: about three hours, late-afternoon start, local English-speaking guide, gallery entry, one drink, walking route, comfortable shoes, camera and sunscreen recommended, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra Flying Dress Experience
tours.description:
The flying dress photograph has become one of the images people bring home from Accra: a long sheet of fabric caught in the air, with the city behind it. This three-hour session supplies the dress, a professional photographer and a location chosen for the shot, so you do not need to find a gown or a studio on your own.

The dress rental is part of the booking, and someone is on hand to help you into it and arrange the fabric before each frame. Your photographer directs the shoot and coaches you through poses, which matters if you have never modelled. The session takes place at a selected location in Accra, with basic props available.

When the shoot is over, you receive professionally edited digital photos.

Pickup is from Station Road in Accra Central. Bring the look you want for hair and make-up, since the booking covers the dress and the photography rather than styling.

Good to know: about three hours, flying dress rental, professional photographer, dressing and posing assistance, edited digital photos, basic props, pickup in Accra Central, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra Food Tasting Tour
tours.description:
Ghanaian food rewards curiosity. The flavours move between smoky, fermented, spicy and sweet, and the best way to understand them is to eat across several dishes in one sitting. This four-hour tasting in Accra is built around your preferences rather than a fixed menu: tell your guide what you eat, or what you would rather avoid, and the selection is adjusted around that.

A dedicated local guide leads the tasting and explains what each dish is, how it is usually eaten and where the ingredients come from. You work through a handpicked range of Ghanaian cooking rather than a greatest-hits plate, with time to ask questions between courses.

Between tastings there are indoor games rooted in local tradition, which gives the afternoon a social shape instead of turning it into a lecture. As the sun goes down, the focus shifts to locally crafted drinks, from refreshing brews to older recipes.

The tour is as much about the people at the table as the food, so come ready to talk, play and eat properly rather than nibble.

Pickup is in Accra.

Good to know: about four hours, dedicated local guide, food tasting, local drinks, indoor games, pickup in Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra Guided City Tour: Cultural and Historical Experience
tours.description:
Six hours is enough to see the Accra that a checklist misses, if the stops are chosen well. This guided city tour moves from the country's political history to its markets and craft workshops, with hotel pickup and an air-conditioned vehicle between stops.

The day starts at the W.E.B. Du Bois Centre, the former home and final resting place of the African-American scholar and Pan-Africanist. You walk the grounds, see the museum and hear how his work connected Ghana to the wider struggle for African unity.

Next is the National Museum of Ghana, where the exhibitions cover the country's cultural heritage, traditional life and historical arc. A guide is useful here: the displays make more sense when someone connects them to the places you have just visited.

The route continues to the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and Mausoleum, dedicated to Ghana's first president, then to Makola Market, one of the busiest trading spaces in Accra. You walk through the stalls with your guide, among fabrics, spices and household goods.

At the Accra Arts Centre you can browse clothing, paintings, beads, carvings and drums made by local artisans. The tour ends at Black Star Square, with the Independence Arch and Black Star Gate, before the drive back to your pickup point.

Bottled water, WiFi on board and the cost of the listed activities are included.

Good to know: about six hours, hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned vehicle, dedicated guide, bottled water, WiFi on board, activity costs included, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra Night Live Experience
tours.description:
Accra after dark runs on a different clock, and finding the right room on the right night is harder than it looks. This six-hour experience gives you a guide who navigates the city's nightlife for you, in a private air-conditioned vehicle with WiFi on board.

The evening opens with a drive through Osu and East Legon while your guide works out what kind of night your group wants. From there the route is tailored: a rooftop cocktail at a place like SkyBar 25, or Afrobeats at a venue like Republic Bar. Those are examples of the range, not a fixed itinerary.

You visit at least two nightlife locations, and your guide handles the door, the timing and the moves between venues so you are not spending the night queueing or negotiating taxis. That is the real value here: the logistics disappear, and you can focus on the music, the fashion and the company.

The tour is designed for travellers who want to see how the city socialises, not just tick off a bar. Tell your guide what you like early and the evening gets better.

Food and drinks are not listed among the inclusions, so budget for what you order at each stop.

The evening starts from Kinbu Street in central Accra.

Good to know: about six hours, knowledgeable guide, private air-conditioned vehicle, WiFi on board, at least two nightlife locations, start from Kinbu Street, food and drinks extra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra: 2-Day Trip to Aqua Safari Resort and Treasure Island
tours.description:
This two-day trip leaves Accra at 6am and heads east to Ada, where the Volta River meets the Atlantic. The drive is part of the experience: you travel in an air-conditioned 4x4 or minivan, with a breakfast pack, water and fresh fruit handed out on the way, and a guide and driver with you throughout.

The first day is based at Aqua Safari Resort. The resort sits on the water and is built for switching off: donkey rides, a boat cruise and a lakeside setting where the pace drops. You have the evening to settle in before the second day.

After an overnight stay, your hotel pickup takes you to Treasure Island in Ada, where the water activities take over. Swimming is the simplest option, with jet skiing and boat cruises for something faster, and segway and horse riding on land. The day ends with the drive back to Accra and drop-off at your hotel.

Entrance fees and pool access are included. Accommodation is not listed among the inclusions, so confirm the room with the operator when you book. Some of the activities on Treasure Island may be priced separately, so check before you commit if budget matters.

This is a good fit for couples, families and small groups who want a short break from the city without arranging transport and logistics themselves.

Good to know: two days, 6am pickup in Accra, air-conditioned 4x4 or minivan, breakfast pack, water and fruit on the drive, guide and driver, Aqua Safari Resort and Treasure Island, entrance fees and pool included, accommodation not listed, return to Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra: Golf Lesson with Optional Dinner and Transfers
tours.description:
This two-hour lesson is for anyone who has wanted to try golf without committing to a club membership, and for players who want a professional to look at a swing that has stopped improving. An instructor works at your pace, starting with the basics if you are new: grip, posture, alignment and the shape of a swing.

If you already play, the session shifts to what is actually costing you shots, whether that is contact, direction or putting. The course is scenic and relaxed rather than tournament-tight, which makes it a comfortable place to learn.

After the lesson you can stay for lunch at the clubhouse or a nearby restaurant, with local and international dishes and views over the course. The meal and transfers from Accra are optional add-ons rather than automatic inclusions, so decide when booking whether you want the lesson on its own or the fuller outing.

It works well for couples, friends and solo travellers, and for anyone who wants a couple of active hours followed by a long lunch.

Good to know: about two hours, professional instructor, equipment fundamentals and swing coaching, optional lunch, optional transfers from Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra: Sankofa Art Gallery Tour & Candle-Making Workshop
tours.description:
This four-hour experience splits neatly in two: a guided look at Ghanaian art, then a workshop where you make something to take home.

The first half is a guided visit to Sankofa Gallery in Accra. You move through work by local artists with a guide who explains the ideas, materials and traditions behind it, and connects the pieces to Ghana's wider history. It is a useful introduction if you are still finding your way into Ghanaian art, and a good place to ask the questions a gallery label does not answer.

The second half is the workshop. A professional team takes you through designing a candle, choosing its scent and pouring it, with locally inspired elements worked into the finish. You leave with the candle you made rather than a shop-bought souvenir.

The experience is designed for art lovers, couples, families, solo travellers and anyone who wants a slower, creative afternoon. Hotel pickup and drop-off, an air-conditioned vehicle, admission fees, the guided activities, bottled water and instruction are all included.

Pickup is from the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City.

Good to know: about four hours, guided gallery visit, hands-on candle-making workshop, candle to take home, hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned vehicle, admission and activities, bottled water, skilled instructor, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra: Shai Hills Safari & Akosombo Boat Cruise Day Tour
tours.description:
This seven-hour day packs three different experiences into one route: a hike and rock climb in Shai Hills, a wildlife drive, and a boat cruise on Lake Volta at Akosombo.

It starts with hotel pickup in Accra and a drive to Shai Hills, where the day opens on foot. The hike follows forest trails and rolling ground, with a rock-climbing section on the reserve's granite formations and views across the savannah. Then you switch to a vehicle for the safari drive, looking for zebras, antelopes and baboons.

The Animal Museum adds context to what you have seen, with displays on Ghana's wildlife and heritage, and the route includes time with local communities.

The afternoon moves to Akosombo and Lake Volta. The boat cruise is the calm counterpoint to the morning: open water, shoreline scenery and a chance to take the wheel and learn how the boat handles. It is a hands-on segment rather than a sit-back tour.

Hotel pickup and drop-off, an air-conditioned vehicle, a guide, bottled water, the safari, rock climbing, museum entry, the boat cruise and activity costs are included.

Bring comfortable shoes for the hike and a towel for the lake.

Good to know: about seven hours, hotel pickup and drop-off in Accra, air-conditioned vehicle, guide, bottled water, Shai Hills hike and rock climbing, safari drive, Animal Museum, community visit, Lake Volta boat cruise, bring comfortable shoes and a towel, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Accra: Traditional African Dance and Drumming Show
tours.description:
Three hours, a room full of drums, and a performance that does not stay on the stage. This traditional African dance and drumming show pairs live percussion and dance with the chance to join in.

The drummers open the performance, building rhythms that the dancers answer with movement. The choreography is storytelling as much as spectacle: gestures and footwork carry meaning, and the show moves between pieces rather than repeating one routine. Dancers perform in colourful, flowing attire, and the energy in the room is closer to a celebration than a theatre performance.

Then the format loosens. You are invited to clap along, try a few steps, and work with a dance instructor if you want to learn more than a shuffle. No experience is needed; join in as much as you like.

Afterwards, a freshly prepared traditional African lunch is served, using seasonal ingredients and recipes that have been passed down rather than adapted for visitors.

Hotel transfers are included, so the day does not depend on finding a taxi home.

Good to know: about three hours, live dance and drumming performance, interactive lesson with a dance instructor, traditional African lunch, hotel transfers, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Ada: day tour with amazing experience
tours.description:
This day trip leaves Accra at 7am and drives to Ada Foah, about an hour and a half to two hours east, where the Volta River spreads into lagoons and the coast. The day is built around culture first and water second.

The morning is spent at the Nkyimkyim Museum, which combines African art and history with live performance. Drumming, dancing, traditional rites and food are part of the programme, and the museum frames the experience around healing and restorative justice, including the legacies of enslavement and colonialism. It is a more reflective stop than a standard heritage tour.

Late morning shifts to a local community, where you spend time with residents and learn how the village lives and works. Then the day moves to Crocodile Island for a boat ride through the calm water, with time for the island's other activities and plenty of photographs.

You return to Accra in the evening. Transport, museum entry, the community visit, the crocodile island boat ride, a guide and entry fees are included.

This tour is sold as final sale: there is no refund, so check your dates before booking. Wear comfortable shoes.

Good to know: about seven hours, 7am departure from Accra, Nkyimkyim Museum, community visit, Crocodile Island boat ride, guide, transport and entry fees, comfortable shoes, no refunds.

tours.title: Akosombo: African spirituality shrine experience
tours.description:
This six-hour trip east of Accra is built around a shrine visit, but it is really about how spiritual life, craft and trade sit together in this part of Ghana. Your guide collects you from your hotel at 8:30am and drives you towards Akosombo.

At the shrine, a custodian explains the beliefs and rituals that shape local worship: ancestral reverence, sacred symbols, and libation, the practice of pouring drink as an offering during prayers, gratitude and community ceremonies. You have time to ask questions and to understand how the practices fit into daily life.

Drumming and dancing follow, and you are invited to watch or join in. The day also includes time with community members, sharing stories and getting a first-hand sense of daily life and the values that hold it together. You also learn about traditional herbs and plants, and how they are used for healing, protection and wellness.

The route continues to Cedi Beads at Odumase Krobo, where recycled glass is turned into handmade beads. You see the full process, learn what beads mean in Ghanaian life, and can make or buy pieces directly from the artisans. A stop at the fresh fruit market at Akuse Junction adds pineapple, mango, watermelon, banana and coconut from nearby farms, with a chance to taste what is in season.

Lunch, snacks, fruit and water are included, and the private vehicle brings you back to Accra at the end.

Good to know: 8:30am pickup, about six hours, private transport and fuel, culture guide, shrine entry and activity fees, lunch, snacks, fruit and water, bring a change of clothes, comfortable clothes and shoes, and a daypack, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Cape Coast Castle and Kakum National Park Day Tour
tours.description:
This is a long day, and it is meant to be. Pickup is at 5:30am in Accra, followed by a three-to-four-hour drive west to Cape Coast, so the first stop at Kakum National Park happens before the heat settles in.

At Kakum you walk the canopy walkway, the suspended route through the rainforest that gives you a view of the forest from above rather than from the trail. It is the gentlest way to see the park and the reason most visitors come.

From there the day turns to history. You drive to Elmina Castle, the Portuguese-built fort that became one of the key points in the transatlantic slave trade, and walk its courtyards and dungeons with a guide who explains what happened there.

After a lunch break, the tour continues to Cape Coast Castle for the same history at a different site, ending at the Door of No Return. The return drive to Accra follows, with arrival in the evening.

Entrance fees, bottled water, an air-conditioned vehicle, a professional guide and pickup and drop-off are included. Wear comfortable shoes; there is a lot of walking on hard ground.

Good to know: about 15 hours door to door, 5:30am pickup, Kakum canopy walkway, Elmina Castle, Cape Coast Castle, lunch break, professional guide, entrance fees, bottled water, air-conditioned vehicle, comfortable shoes, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Cape Coast Castle, Elmina Castle & Kakum National Park Tour
tours.description:
This eleven-hour tour covers the three sites most visitors to Cape Coast want to see, in a single route from Accra: the Kakum canopy walkway, Elmina Castle and Cape Coast Castle.

The drive from Accra takes about three hours. The first stop is Kakum National Park, where the canopy walkway crosses seven bridges suspended above the rainforest. The walk is the easiest way to see the forest's upper level, and the views open up between the platforms.

Then the day moves to Elmina Castle, or St George's Castle, the first European-built structure in sub-Saharan Africa. A guide takes you through the courtyards and slave dungeons and explains the castle's role in the transatlantic trade.

The final stop is Cape Coast Castle, with its dungeons and museum, and the wider story of Cape Coast as Ghana's first capital. The return drive to Accra follows.

Bottled water, a dedicated guide, hotel pickup and drop-off, WiFi on board, an air-conditioned vehicle and the cost of the listed activities are included.

The day is heavy on history and light on shade, so bring water and wear shoes you can stand in for long stretches.

Good to know: about eleven hours, three-hour drive from Accra, Kakum canopy walkway, Elmina Castle, Cape Coast Castle and museum, hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned vehicle, guide, bottled water, WiFi on board, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Chale walking tours (walking tours in James Town community)
tours.description:
James Town is one of Accra's oldest quarters, and this one-hour walk stays close to the water and the people who work it. The route starts in the fishing village, where canoes are pulled up on the beach and the day's catch is being handled, and moves through streets that most visitors pass without stopping.

At a family house you learn how the household is organised and what everyday customs look like, rather than hearing a general history of Ghana. The walk then continues to the beach, where you meet fisherfolk and hear how the trade works from the people doing it.

There is food and drink along the way: local snacks, millet beer and akpeteshie, the palm-nut spirit distilled in the region. The walk also takes in the underground dungeons and the old forts along the coast, with a guide explaining the history of the site and the community around it.

Entry fees, water and transport are included. Bring cash for anything you want to buy, and wear comfortable clothes and shoes for walking.

Good to know: about one hour, James Town fishing village, family house visit, beach and fisherfolk, local snacks and drinks, dungeons and forts, guide, entry fees, water and transport included, bring cash and comfortable clothes, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: From Accra : Waterfalls, Aburi Gardens & Cocoa Farm Tour
tours.description:
This full day out of Accra climbs into the Akuapem Mountains, where the temperature drops and the roads start to switchback. The first stop is Aburi Botanical Gardens, one of Ghana's oldest planted landscapes, with tropical trees, paths and a guide who explains what you are looking at.

From there the route continues to the Tetteh Quarshie Cocoa Farm, the place tied to the introduction of cocoa to Ghana. You see how the crop is grown, harvested and processed, and hear how it became central to the country's economy and everyday life.

The afternoon belongs to water. Depending on the season, access and conditions on the day, the tour visits Boti Falls, Akaa Falls or Asenema Falls, all set in forest. The exact fall is chosen for the best experience that day, so the itinerary is confirmed rather than fixed months in advance.

The day also includes a hike to Umbrella Rock, the natural formation that gives a wide view over the surrounding hills, before the drive back to Accra.

Hotel or Airbnb pickup and drop-off in Accra, an air-conditioned vehicle, a guide, WiFi on board, bottled water and entrance fees with guided tours at each stop are included.

Bring water, a charged phone, cash, comfortable clothes and shoes, and a power bank.

Good to know: about seven hours, pickup and drop-off in Accra, air-conditioned vehicle, guide, WiFi, bottled water, Aburi Botanical Gardens, Tetteh Quarshie Cocoa Farm, one waterfall (Boti, Akaa or Asenema), Umbrella Rock hike, entrance fees included, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: From Accra: The Nature Escape Adventure
tours.description:
This two-day trip leaves Accra and loops through the Volta Region, combining wildlife, water and a mountain hike without asking you to arrange the pieces yourself.

The first day starts at Shai Hills Resource Reserve, where the savannah and granite outcrops are a sharp change from the coast. From there the route continues to Lake Volta for a boat cruise, with the afternoon given over to the water and the shoreline.

Later you visit the Tafi Monkey Sanctuary, where Mona monkeys move through the forest and are accustomed enough to be watched at close range. The day ends with accommodation arranged as part of the package.

The second day is the physical one. You walk through tropical forest to Wli Waterfalls, the tallest in Ghana, and then hike Mount Afadjato for the view over the surrounding mountains, valleys and communities. The return drive to Accra follows.

Private air-conditioned transport, a professional guide, accommodation, hotel pickup and drop-off, entrance fees and scheduled activities are included. WiFi is available on board where the network allows. Bring comfortable shoes; the waterfall walk and the mountain are both on foot.

Good to know: two days, Volta Region, Shai Hills, Lake Volta boat cruise, Tafi Monkey Sanctuary, Wli Waterfalls, Mount Afadjato hike, private transport and guide, accommodation, hotel pickup and drop-off, WiFi subject to network, comfortable shoes, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Kotoka International Airport (ACC): Lounge Entry
tours.description:
A three-hour lounge pass for Kotoka International Airport, useful when you arrive early or have a long connection and do not want to spend it in the departures hall.

The Adinkra Lounge is run by a third-party operator and sits before customs and immigration, so you can use it without leaving the terminal. Inside there is seating, WiFi and charging points, international television, newspapers and magazines, and flight information so you can keep an eye on your gate.

Food and drinks are available to buy rather than included in the pass. If you want to work, the WiFi and power make that straightforward; if you would rather eat and sit quietly, the lounge is set up for that too.

Bring your booking voucher. Entry is for three hours, and the pass is sold as final sale, with no refunds.

Good to know: three hours of lounge access, Adinkra Lounge, before customs and immigration, seating, WiFi and charging, international TV, newspapers and magazines, flight information, food and drinks available to buy, bring your booking voucher, no refunds.

tours.title: Private Accra International Airport Pickup & Dropoff
tours.description:
This is an airport transfer with a short introduction to Accra built in. A driver meets you at arrivals with a name board, helps with luggage and takes you to a private air-conditioned vehicle, so the first hour after landing does not involve negotiating a taxi.

The route includes Independence Square, where the Black Star Gate and the independence story give the city some context, and the Accra Arts Centre, where you can browse crafts and souvenirs before continuing to your accommodation.

Bottled water and WiFi are on board, and the driver is there to answer questions about the city, food and what to see during your stay. It is a useful first orientation if you have not been to Accra before.

The service is private, so the vehicle is yours rather than shared, and drop-off is at your hotel or accommodation. The same service can be booked in reverse for departure.

Good to know: about three hours including the short city route, meet and greet at arrivals, private air-conditioned vehicle, professional driver, luggage assistance, bottled water, WiFi on board, Independence Square and Accra Arts Centre, drop-off at your accommodation, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Safari Valley: Aburi Safari Valley Eco Resort Day Tour
tours.description:
Safari Valley is an eco-resort in the Akuapem hills, and this day trip is built around using the whole estate rather than sitting by one pool. Transport from Accra and a guided tour in an electric cart are included, so you see the scale of the place before choosing how to spend the rest of the day.

The cart tour takes in the eco-park and zoo, with animals in open surroundings and a guide explaining the resort's approach to the land. From there the choice is yours: walking and jogging trails, bicycle or segway rides, archery, table tennis, petanque, bowling, darts, board games, swimming, water aerobics, football, the gym, nine-hole golf, basketball, volleyball, badminton, lawn tennis, horse riding and a children's amusement park are all on site.

Lunch is a three-to-five-course meal made from produce grown on the farm, served with freshly squeezed fruit juice. It is a proper sit-down break rather than a snack, and the pace of the day is designed around it.

The resort suits families, couples and groups who want a mix of activities and quiet, with the option to do very little if that is the mood.

Good to know: about eight hours, transport from Accra, guided electric-cart tour, eco-park and zoo, three-to-five-course farm lunch with fresh juice, full activity list including swimming, golf, tennis, horse riding and a children's park, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The Agbogbloshie Accra E-waste & Recycling Experience
tours.description:
Most visitors see Accra through its forts, markets and beaches. This four-hour experience goes to Agbogbloshie, one of the world's largest informal e-waste processing sites, and looks directly at what happens to discarded electronics.

The tour begins with a briefing on the global e-waste trade, Ghana's place in the recycling chain and how Agbogbloshie changed from wetland to a place where devices from around the world are dismantled. That context matters: without it, the site is easy to misread.

You then walk the area with local guides and community members. You watch the methods workers use to recover metals and reusable parts from old equipment, and you meet some of the people who earn a living there. Their accounts are the centre of the experience, not background colour.

The route also follows the Odaw River, where the environmental cost of unregulated disposal is visible, and your guide explains the remediation work under way and the alternatives being discussed. The tour ends with a conversation about local innovation and the practical choices consumers can make.

It is a private tour with private transport and hotel pickup and drop-off in Accra, so the day is handled door to door.

Come with questions. This is an educational visit, and the conversations are better when you engage with them.

Good to know: about four hours, private tour and transport, local guides, entry fees, hotel pickup and drop-off in Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The Cape Coast Day tour with Assin Manso Slave River bath
tours.description:
This eleven-hour tour adds Assin Manso to the usual Cape Coast route, which changes the day from a visit to two castles into a wider account of the slave trade's geography.

The first stop is Cape Coast Castle. A guide takes you through the dungeons and fortifications and explains the castle's role in the transatlantic trade, with the history presented directly rather than softened.

From there you continue to Elmina Castle, built by the Portuguese in the fifteenth century and one of the oldest European buildings in sub-Saharan Africa. The visit covers its role in the trade and the wider history of the coast.

The route then turns inland to the Assin Manso Slave River site, where enslaved Africans were bathed before being marched to the coast. The site includes a memorial, and the stop is quieter and more reflective than the castles.

The day ends at Kakum National Park, walking the canopy walkway above the rainforest floor. It is a complete change of register after the historical sites, and a good way to close a heavy day.

A private guide, hotel pickup and drop-off, WiFi on board and an air-conditioned vehicle are included.

Good to know: about eleven hours, Cape Coast Castle, Elmina Castle, Assin Manso Slave River and memorial, Kakum canopy walkway, private guide, hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned vehicle, WiFi on board, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The Despite Automobile Museum
tours.description:
The Despite Automobile Museum in East Legon is Ghana's first automobile museum, and the collection is broader than the word "museum" might suggest: vintage and classic cars, luxury vehicles and modern performance models, displayed together rather than in separate rooms.

The exhibits trace how design, engineering and comfort changed across the decades. Cars that many visitors have only seen in films or magazines are here in the metal, and the educational displays explain the craftsmanship and technology behind them. It is as useful for students and families as for people who already know their engines.

You can walk the collection independently or choose a guided walkthrough for more detail on individual vehicles and their histories. Museum staff are on hand for questions.

A few rules matter: photography is not allowed inside the exhibition areas, visitors must not touch or lean on the cars, and food and drink are not permitted in the exhibit spaces.

The museum is at 200 Cotton Street, East Legon, and opens daily from 10am to 8pm, with visits organised into limited hourly sessions. Advance reservations are recommended, and you need to show your booking confirmation on arrival.

Good to know: about three hours, Ghana's first automobile museum, East Legon, vintage, classic, luxury and modern cars, optional guided walkthrough, admission and staff assistance, open daily 10am-8pm, hourly sessions, advance booking recommended, no photography inside, do not touch the vehicles, no food or drink in the exhibit spaces.

tours.title: The Ghana Naming Ceremony Tour
tours.description:
Ghanaian names are rarely just labels. In many communities a name records the day you were born, the circumstances of your arrival, or a quality your family hopes you will carry. This six-hour experience lets you take part in a traditional naming ceremony rather than watch one from a distance.

Your guide collects you from your hotel in Accra and drives you to the ceremony in an air-conditioned vehicle. On arrival you are welcomed by the community hosting the day. You hear the prayers and music that are part of the ceremony, and see the dancing that turns it into a celebration rather than a formal rite.

Then comes the part most visitors remember: receiving your own Ghanaian name. Your host explains how names are chosen, whether from the day of the week you were born, from family heritage, or from personal qualities, and you receive a certificate recording the name.

Food and drinks are served as part of the day, and there is time to talk with the people around you, ask questions about what you have seen, and understand what it means to be formally welcomed into the community.

Good to know: about six hours, private guide, hotel pickup and drop-off in Accra, air-conditioned vehicle, WiFi on board, food and drinks included, naming certificate, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The Ghanaian cultural and Heritage Tour
tours.description:
This is a six-day private cultural tour rather than a city break with a few stops attached. The route brings together the parts of Ghana that are hardest to arrange independently: a naming ceremony, a night out in Accra, the kente weavers of Bonwire, a craft and Adinkra workshop, and the royal history of Manhyia Palace in Kumasi.

In Accra the itinerary covers the city's landmarks, including Independence Square and the Accra Arts Centre, where crafts, fabrics, artwork and souvenirs are sold by the people who make them. The naming ceremony is the personal centrepiece: you take part in the rituals, receive a Ghanaian name and learn what it means.

The tour also includes an Accra night out, which gives the trip a social side beyond the daytime visits.

Outside the capital, the route goes to Bonwire, the weaving village associated with kente, where the cloth is made on traditional looms. A craft and Adinkra symbols village adds the visual language behind Ghanaian textiles, and the Manhyia Palace Museum in Kumasi covers the Ashanti royal line, its leadership and its role in the country's history.

Private transport, an air-conditioned vehicle, a private guide, snacks, bottled water and WiFi are included, with the round trip starting and ending in Accra.

This is a multi-day booking: confirm the day-by-day schedule and accommodation arrangements with the operator before you pay, since accommodation is not listed among the inclusions.

Good to know: six days, private transport and guide, Accra landmarks, naming ceremony, Accra nightlife, Bonwire kente village, craft and Adinkra village, Manhyia Palace Museum, snacks and bottled water, WiFi, round trip from Accra, accommodation not listed as included.

tours.title: The Kumasi Cultural and Heritage Day Tour
tours.description:
Kumasi is a long day from Accra, but it is the only way to see the Ashanti Kingdom's political and cultural heart without staying overnight. The drive takes the morning, and the route then works through four sites that together explain the kingdom's history.

The first is Manhyia Palace Museum, the residence and cultural home of the Asantehene. The exhibits cover the Ashanti leadership system, the role of kings and queen mothers, and the royal artefacts and photographs that document the line.

From there you visit the Okomfo Anokye Sword Site, where a sacred sword is said to have been planted in the ground by the Ashanti priest Okomfo Anokye. The story behind it is a lesson in how the kingdom's unity is remembered.

The Prempeh II Museum adds royal regalia, traditional clothing and ceremonial objects, before the tour moves to Kejetia Market, one of the largest open-air markets in West Africa. The scale is the point: fabrics, crafts, food, jewellery and household goods spread through the stalls.

The final stop is the Bonwire Kente Weaving Centre, where weavers work traditional looms. You see how the cloth is made and what the colours and patterns mean, and can buy directly from the workshop.

Private transport, an air-conditioned vehicle, a guide and entry to the sites are included. It is a full twelve-hour day, so expect an early start and a late return.

Good to know: about twelve hours, Manhyia Palace Museum, Okomfo Anokye Sword Site, Prempeh II Museum, Kejetia Market, Bonwire Kente Weaving Centre, private transport and guide, entry fees included, round trip from Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The Mole National Park Tour
tours.description:
Mole National Park is Ghana's largest protected wildlife area, and this two-day trip is built around seeing it properly rather than passing through. The park's savannah, woodland and watering holes support elephants, antelopes, warthogs, baboons, monkeys and a long list of bird species.

The safari is led by local guides who know where the animals are likely to be and can explain the behaviour and ecology behind what you see. Early morning and late afternoon are the most productive windows, when the heat eases and the animals move.

You can explore by 4x4 or on a guided walking safari, depending on the option you choose. The walking version is slower and more immersive: you notice tracks, vegetation and smaller wildlife that a vehicle passes. Elephants are often seen at a safe distance around water sources.

The landscape is part of the appeal, with wide views over the northern savannah and space to photograph without a crowd. It is a different Ghana from the coast, and the trip is timed to give you time in the park rather than a rushed game drive.

Accommodation, private transport, an air-conditioned vehicle, a private guide, hotel pickup and drop-off and WiFi are included. Meals are not listed among the inclusions, so budget for food separately.

Good to know: two days, Mole National Park, guided 4x4 or walking safari, elephants and other wildlife, birdwatching, accommodation, private transport and guide, hotel pickup and drop-off, WiFi, meals not listed as included, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: The North Safari
tours.description:
This overnight safari in northern Ghana combines Mole National Park with the village life and architecture around it, rather than treating the park as a standalone game drive.

The wildlife comes first. A walking safari puts you on the ground with a guide, tracking elephants, baboons, antelopes and other animals at a pace a vehicle cannot match. A jeep safari covers more ground and reaches the open savannah where the larger herds gather.

From Mole the route moves to Mognori Eco-Village for a canoe safari on the Mole River. The water is quiet, the birdlife is close, and the visit includes time with the community and a look at how shea butter is made.

The final stop is the Larabanga Mosque, a Sudanese-style building dating from 1421 and one of the oldest mosques in West Africa. It is a working religious site as well as a historical one, and the visit is guided.

Accommodation is en-suite and air-conditioned, with breakfast included. The package also covers an air-conditioned vehicle, all fees and taxes, two walking and jeep safaris, and entry to the park, Larabanga and Mognori.

This is an overnight trip: you sleep near the park and continue the next day, so pack for a night away. The tour is sold as final sale, with no refunds.

Good to know: two days, one night, Mole National Park, walking and jeep safaris, canoe safari at Mognori Eco-Village, Larabanga Mosque, shea butter making, en-suite air-conditioned accommodation with breakfast, all fees and taxes, comfortable shoes, no refunds.

tours.title: The Shia Hills Safari Quad-Bike Tour
tours.description:
Shai Hills Resource Reserve sits in the Greater Accra Region, close enough to the city for a day trip but different enough to feel like a break from it. This seven-hour tour explores the reserve on a quad bike, with a private guide and hotel pickup in Accra.

The ride follows tracks through the reserve's savannah and granite outcrops, with stops for the views and for wildlife. Monkeys, baboons, antelopes and a range of birdlife live here, and the reserve's rock formations are a feature in their own right.

Because the tour is private, the pace is set by your group. You can spend longer at a viewpoint or a wildlife sighting without holding up another vehicle, and the guide can adjust the route to what you want from the day.

Breakfast is included, along with an air-conditioned vehicle, WiFi on board, a private guide and hotel pickup and drop-off. The pickup area covers Nima and central Accra.

Bring clothes you do not mind getting dusty and shoes with grip. The reserve is a natural site, not a theme park, and the terrain is part of the experience.

Good to know: about seven hours, quad-bike ride through Shai Hills Resource Reserve in the Greater Accra Region, wildlife and rock formations, private guide, hotel pickup and drop-off in Accra, air-conditioned vehicle, WiFi, breakfast included, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Traditional Beadmaking Workshop
tours.description:
Glass beads are one of Ghana's older crafts, and this workshop teaches the process from the raw material up. Broken bottles are pounded, kneaded and baked in a mud oven before they become beads, and you work through those stages yourself rather than watching a demonstration.

The session runs for about four hours inside a seven-hour day from Accra. An instructor explains each step, answers questions about the tools and the skills behind them, and helps you choose a style: wrist, ankle or neck beads. You leave with the piece you made.

Waist beads are not part of the workshop because they take longer to make than the session allows. If you want a set, you can buy a finished one from the showroom or choose colours, sizes and shapes for the beadmaker to arrange for you.

Photos and videos are allowed while you work, so bring a camera or use your phone. You also get souvenirs to take home as mementos.

Private air-conditioned transport, a guide, bottled water and the workshop fee are included. Pickup is in Accra.

Good to know: about four hours in the workshop and seven hours door to door, private air-conditioned transport, guide, workshop fees, bottled water, pickup in Accra, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Transport form Accra to Cape Coast
tours.description:
A private transfer from Accra to Cape Coast, for travellers who want the journey handled without joining a group bus or negotiating at the roadside.

The driver meets you at your hotel, residence or agreed pickup point in Accra, helps with luggage and sets off west in a clean, air-conditioned vehicle. The drive usually takes three to four hours depending on traffic and road conditions, with views of markets, countryside and the coast along the way.

The service is private, so the vehicle is yours. Short stops can be arranged for refreshments, a restroom or to stretch your legs, and the pickup time can be set around your plans. An early departure is worth considering if you want more time in Cape Coast and a easier run out of Accra.

Drop-off is at your destination in Cape Coast, whether that is a hotel, a sight, or the start of a longer trip. The transfer also works for visitors heading to Cape Coast Castle, Elmina Castle, Kakum National Park, Assin Manso or the beaches.

Fuel, the vehicle, the driver, bottled water and luggage assistance are included. When booking, give your pickup location, preferred departure time, number of travellers, luggage details and final destination.

Good to know: about ten hours including the drive and stops, private air-conditioned vehicle, professional driver, pickup in Accra, drop-off in Cape Coast, luggage assistance, bottled water, fuel included, optional stops, flexible pickup times, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: Waterfalls Massage With Aburi Gardens & Cocoa Farm Activity
tours.description:
This seven-hour trip out of Accra combines two gentle visits with a massage beside a waterfall, which is a more unusual way to end a day in the Aburi hills than the usual drive back to the city.

The first stop is Aburi Botanical Gardens, where paths run through tropical planting and mature trees. A guide covers the garden's history and the plants that made it one of Ghana's oldest botanical collections.

From there you continue to the Tetteh Quarshie Cocoa Farm, the site tied to the introduction of cocoa to Ghana. You see how the crop is grown and processed and hear how it shaped the country's economy and communities.

The final stop is a waterfall in the surrounding forest. A professional therapist sets up beside the cascading water for a massage, with the sound of the falls as the backdrop. It is a simple setup rather than a spa, and that is part of the appeal.

Hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned transport, a guide, entry to the gardens, cocoa farm and waterfall, the massage session, bottled water, WiFi on board and the listed activities are included.

Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, beachwear, cash and a charged phone.

Good to know: about seven hours, Aburi Botanical Gardens, Tetteh Quarshie Cocoa Farm, waterfall massage with a professional therapist, hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned transport, guide, all entries, bottled water, WiFi, bring swimwear and a change of clothes, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

tours.title: World Heritage fortresses and Nzulezo
tours.description:
This route along Ghana's western coast pairs four little-visited fortresses with Nzulezo, the village built on stilts above a lake. It starts from Cape Coast between 6 and 8am and travels west through Sekondi-Takoradi.

The first stop is Busua, where the Atlantic is calm enough for a swim. From there the route continues to Fort Metal Cross at Dixcove, built by the British in the seventeenth century, and to the Prussian fort at Awiabo Aiyinase, a reminder that this coast was contested by several European powers.

The day ends at Beyin, the gateway to Nzulezo. The village can only be reached by small boat, and life there takes place on wooden planks and raffia-palm stilts above the lake. Around 500 people live in the community, fishing and farming as their families have for centuries, though modern life has left its mark. You can walk the walkways, visit a school or place of worship, and eat freshly fried fish.

You can return to Cape Coast the same evening, or take the optional overnight in a guest house on the lake. With the overnight, the next morning includes Fort Apollonia in Beyin and an introduction to Nzema culture, then Fort St Anthony in Axim, built by the Portuguese in 1515, before the drive back.

The listed duration is 10 hours for the day version; the overnight is an add-on, so confirm the return time and the room with the operator when you book.

Good to know: 10 hours as a day trip, optional overnight in a Nzulezo guest house, pickup from Cape Coast, Busua swim, Fort Metal Cross, Fort Gross Friedrichsburg, Nzulezo stilt village by boat, Fort Apollonia, Fort St Anthony, small group of 1-7, air-conditioned transport, guide, bring swimwear, sunscreen, insect repellent, toiletries and a daypack, free cancellation up to 24 hours before.
